stem: Mehak mixes fine dry sand with iron filings. She can still see both the sand grains and the dark filings. A magnet pulls out the filings; the sand stays behind.

options.text: The sample is a mixture: sand and iron filings are physically mixed and each keeps its own properties.
The sample is not a mixture because two different solids are present.
Only pure substances can be components of a mixture, so this sample cannot be a mixture.
The sample is a mixture only after the magnet is used.

teacher.key_rationale: A mixture forms when substances are mixed without a chemical reaction and keep their own properties. Sand and iron filings do that from the moment they are mixed; two solids can be components, and separation with a magnet is not required to make it a mixture.
